name: Familial Porphyria Cutanea Tarda

criteria.description: Elevated urinary uroporphyrin and other porphyrins
Reduced hepatic uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase enzyme activity
Chronic blistering photosensitive skin lesions on sun-exposed areas
Positive family history of porphyria cutanea tarda
Evidence of hepatic iron overload or elevated serum ferritin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated urinary porphyrins, reduced hepatic UROD activity, and characteristic cutaneous blistering lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for UROD mutations supports diagnosis in familial cases

pathognomonic.symptomName: Photosensitive blistering on dorsal hands and forearms
pathognomonic.notes: Blisters develop after sun exposure, often with minimal trauma
searchTerms: blistering skin on back of hands and forearms when exposed to light
photosensitive skin blisters on dorsal hands

pathognomonic.symptomName: Skin fragility with erosions and scarring
searchTerms: fragile skin with erosions and scars
skin fragility causing wounds and scars

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypertrichosis of facial and upper body regions
searchTerms: excessive facial and upper body hair
unusual hair growth on face and chest
thick hair on face and upper body
small white bumps on sun-exposed skin
white skin bumps from sun exposure
skin that feels tight and firm

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to porphyrin neurotoxicity
rare.notes: Rare in PCT but reported in severe cases
searchTerms: nerve damage causing weakness or numbness

laboratory: Elevated urinary and plasma uroporphyrins and heptacarboxyl porphyrins
Reduced hepatic uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase enzyme activity
Elevated liver transaminases and serum ferritin
imaging: Liver ultrasound or MRI may show hepatomegaly or cirrhotic changes
other: Positive family history of porphyria cutanea tarda
Photosensitivity testing may reproduce skin lesions

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with acquired risk factors such as alcohol use, hepatitis C, or iron overload
Blistering from mechanical trauma without photosensitivity
Similar skin findings without porphyrin abnormalities

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin blistering with secondary infection
Signs of liver failure or cirrhosis
references: Anderson KE, Sassa S, Bishop DF, Desnick RJ. Disorders of Heme Biosynthesis: X-Linked Sideroblastic Anemia and the Porphyrias. In: Scriver CR, et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
Balwani M, Desnick RJ. The porphyrias: advances in diagnosis and treatment. Blood. 2012;120(23):4496-504.
